Play a recorded lattice run back in the browser

Source: R/spatial-view.R
abm_view_lattice.Rd

abm_plot_lattice() draws one frame; abm_view_lattice() writes every recorded frame into a single HTML file that plays them back: a canvas of the lattice, play / pause, a tick slider, a speed control, a legend with the counts at the current tick, and a readout of whatever cell or agent the pointer is over. The file is self-contained (its script, style and data are inline; nothing is fetched), so it opens from disk, attaches to an email and works on a phone. It follows the browser's light or dark theme and has a switch of its own.

Usage

abm_view_lattice(
  result,
  fill = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  agents = FALSE,
  colour = NULL,
  mark = NULL,
  hover = NULL,
  tick = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  fill_colours = NULL,
  agent_colours = NULL,
  mark_colours = NULL,
  fps = 8
)

Arguments

result

An abm_run() result, or any data frame carrying .x and .y (for example several final frames bound together with a column saying which run each came from, to facet on).

fill

What colours a cell: a column or an expression over the cell's columns. A logical, character or factor value gets one colour per level; a number gets a gradient (quantised to 64 steps). NULL draws the cells in a neutral grey, for agents to stand on.

file

Where to write the HTML. NULL writes to a temporary file. The path is returned invisibly either way.

agents

Whether to draw the mobile agents over the cells.

colour

What colours a mobile agent: a column or an expression over the agent's columns. .group by default.

mark

Cells to mark over the fill: a character or factor expression over the cell's columns whose levels are the marks and whose NA is no mark, for example case_when(nest ~ "nest", food > 0 ~ "food").

hover

Names of further columns to show in the readout: a cell's columns are stored as quantised layers, an agent's as its values at each tick. Keep it to a few; each one costs as much as the fill does.

tick

Which ticks to play. Every recorded tick by default.

title, subtitle

The page's heading. The title defaults to the fill expression.

labels

What to call the fill, colour and mark values in the legend and the readout, as a character vector named by those three: for example c(fill = "grass height") when fill is an expression.

fill_colours, agent_colours, mark_colours

The colours of the fill, the agents and the marks, as colours in abm_plot_lattice(): a vector named by level, or the stops of a gradient for a numeric value. NULL picks Okabe-Ito colours, or a light-to-blue gradient.

fps

Frames per second at speed 1.

Value

The path of the file, invisibly.

Details

The frames are the ticks abm_run() recorded (record = "all" or a number), so the file grows with the lattice, the number of frames and the number of agents. Cell values are quantised to at most 64 levels and run-length encoded, and an agent costs a few bytes a tick, so a 50 x 50 lattice over 200 frames is well under a megabyte. Thin a long run with record = or tick = rather than recording every tick of it.

See also

abm_plot_lattice() for a static frame of the same result.

Examples

life <- abm_setup(agents = abm_grid(dims = c(30, 30), alive = ~runif(n) < 0.3))
go <- abm_go(abm_neighbours(k ~ sum(alive)),
             abm_rules(alive ~ k == 3 | (alive & k == 2)))
r <- abm_run(life, go, ticks = 30, seed = 1)
f <- abm_view_lattice(r, fill = alive, title = "Game of Life",
                      file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"))
# browseURL(f)   # open it in the browser
